page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highmem-16-lssd is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor with x86_64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores, supporting multithreading with 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 128 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. Storage is bundled via a single local NVMe SSD with a capacity of 402 GB, while GPU acceleration is absent.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench text processing scoring in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance, software compilation, and database operations fall within the average range. However, memory bandwidth exhibits notable bottlenecks; while cached small-block reads are average at 1132.73 GB/sec, uncached large-block read and write bandwidths are weak to poor, dropping to 38.2 GB/sec and 13.16 GB/sec respectively. Large-model LLM inference is also poor, though small-model text generation remains strong.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a high density of memory and local NVMe storage relative to its vCPU count, making it a resource-dense option for memory-bound workloads. The combination of dedicated AMD EPYC cores, 128 GB of RAM, and fast local SSD storage makes this server well-suited for database hosting, in-memory caching systems like Redis, text processing pipelines, and general-purpose workloads requiring high memory capacity without massive parallel compute requirements.
